notes: Later flowering lowers predation; male allocation tracks high predation; selection on perfect-flower production reverses across the environmental ordering.
Larger showy bracts increase bee visitation/pollen arrival and seed-predator exposure; antagonist selection counteracts pollinator selection and net selection tends to stabilizing.
Natural calyx length shows opposing pollination- and seed-predation-mediated selection on a common seed-fitness scale; randomized calyx manipulation and an explicit alternative worldline are absent.

Large flowers provide reproductive benefit but carry drought-related water costs; watering changes demographic consequences but no explicit shared-versus-alternative architecture ordering is recovered.

Attraction/reward coordinates affect pollinator service and hawkmoth oviposition; defence-like reproductive surfaces and flower-specific defence biology exist but the required same-experiment common-scale shared-versus-alternative ordering is missing.

Pollinator and antagonist selection on display morphs varies among years/populations and grazer manipulation shifts morph frequencies; frequency dependence can maintain polymorphism but belongs outside static BALANCE unless worldline ordering is separately identified.

Adding herbivory redirects bee-driven evolutionary trajectories but the antagonist is a leaf herbivore and the experiment does not identify a shared-versus-differentiated architecture fitness ordering.

Bifunctional/generalist and duplicated/specialized outcomes exist under multifunctional demand but replicate lineages include both generalist and specialist trajectories and do not identify one static BALANCE boundary.

Functional partitioning with residual integration is a useful architecture boundary anchor but comparable shared-versus-differentiated fitness and the causal conflict route are not directly identified.

One- and two-active-copy constructs were evolved under selection for both fluorescence colors; duplication made specialization structurally available yet no copy-specific green/blue specialization was recovered.
Precise coding and promoter replacements linked duplication and specialization to resolution of a bifunctional regulatory conflict and organismal fitness improvement in the GAL switch.

Pollen-only buzz-pollinated Solanum mostly retain equal stamens but heteranthery evolved independently multiple times; Solanum rostratum experiments confirm differentiated feeding and pollinating anther functions.

The same 1:1 generalist ancestor shifted rapidly toward asymmetric specialist CNVs under static single-nitrogen limitation while fluctuating glutamine/proline limitation maintained balanced generalist CNVs; genotype fitness was environment-dependent but the study remains a preprint and does not directly estimate optimized WS versus WD across one continuous control path.
